drafts.title: What winter does to my charging bill (AP1, MAIN)
drafts.window: Mon 1 PM MT (main), or Tue 11 AM.
drafts.angle: cold weather raises the bill a little; preheat while plugged in. Cost angle, not a range repeat.
bullets: DOE/EPA: at 20F with heater on, range drops ~41% mixed; heater off ~12% (Level Two Club).
US average rate: 1,000 miles/mo ~$53 mild weather to ~$90 at 20F with heat; 3-month cold snap adds a bit over $110.
Colorado ~17c: 1,000 miles ~$53/mo before winter (NeoCharge).
Biggest fix: preheat cabin and battery while plugged in so the wall pays.
Pixel: garage, show scheduled preconditioning: "Two taps the night before."
Reply target: big EV owner account with first-frost range screenshots, or Sawyer Merritt winter tip.
drafts.body:
$53 a month to drive 1,000 miles in my EV when the weather is nice. Winter can push that toward $90 if you heat the cabin from the pack.

Last January my Tesla app said [kWh used in January: ___]. That is the number that matters, not a scary range screenshot.

My cold-morning trick is simple. I schedule preconditioning the night before so the car warms up in the garage while it is still plugged in. The wall pays for the heat. The battery keeps its juice for the drive.

If you skip that and crank heat on a cold pack, you burn miles twice: once for the cabin, once for the road.

What is your cold-morning trick? Preheat, heated seats only, or just tough it out?

drafts.title: If anyone tells you to pay with a barcode, hang up (AP6, GROWTH)
drafts.window: Mon 11 AM MT, or Tue 11 AM.
drafts.angle: newest gift-card scam twist with cloned kid voice; one calm rule. Different from Oct 6 grandson-voice and Oct 10 fake-FBI posts.
bullets: SSA OIG: caller claims to be police/federal agent; child in jail; may hear cloned voice.
Then barcode/QR to load money at a store and read the code back.
No agency or police takes payment by barcode/QR. Hang up; call official site number.
Report: ssa.gov/scam, 1-800-269-0271, reportfraud.ftc.gov.
Stop Scams Together: >70% of seniors get a scam attempt daily; avg loss $38,000.
Pixel: 20 sec to camera: "If anyone asks you to pay with a barcode, hang up."
Reply target: DogeDesigner or big scam-warning account.
drafts.body:
$38,000. That is the average loss when an older person gets scammed.

The new trick is mean. You get a call that sounds like your kid. Or like a cop. Then they text a barcode or QR code and tell you to load money onto it at a big store and read the code back.

Here is the only rule that matters. No cop. No agency. Nobody from the government takes payment by barcode or QR code. Ever.

Hang up. Call the real number from the official website, not the number they just gave you.

My family's rule is [our rule: ___]. What is yours? Send this to someone who needs it.

drafts.window: Tue 11 AM MT, or Mon 1 PM if F1 slips.

bullets: Stanford SIEPR/NBER: avg worker puts AI job-loss chance in 2 years at ~20%; AI users ~25%.

Fear highest when AI is core of the work (e.g. programming).

drafts.body:
About 20%. That is the chance the average worker thinks AI takes their job in the next two years.

People who already use AI at work put it even higher, about 25%.

The study looked for the layoffs. They have not shown up in a clear way yet. Job postings in the most exposed roles have not crashed either.

That does not mean nothing is changing. Entry-level hiring is getting harder in some fields. Work is reshuffling. Fear is real.

I use AI for [what I use it for: ___] and it made my day easier, not shorter. I am not a tech guy. I just ask it to explain things and save me time.
